definition: Aalenian Age is a division of geological time within the Jurassic Period. It is the first of the four ages within the Mid Jurassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Toarcian Age (Early Jurassic Epoch) and succeeded by the Bajocian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Abereiddian Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of two stages of the Llanvirn Series. It is preceded by the Fennian Stage (Arenig Series) and succeeded by the Llandeilian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Actonian Substage is a substage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of two substages of the Streffordian Stage. It is preceded by the Marshbrookian Substage (Cheneyan Stage) and succeeded by the Onnian Substage (BGS Research Report RR/12/04, table 1).

Aeronian Age is a division of geological time within the Silurian Period. It is the second of the three ages within the Llandovery Epoch. It is preceded by the Rhuddanian Age and succeeded by the Telychian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 21.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Albian Age is a division of geological time within the Cretaceous Period. It is the last of the six ages within the Early Cretaceous Epoch. It is preceded by the Aptian Age and succeeded by the Cenomanian Age (Late Cretaceous Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Alportian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the fourth of seven substages of the Namurian Stage. It is preceded by the Chokierian Substage and succeeded by the Kinderscoutian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Anglian Stage is a Mid Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a cold (glacial) interval. It is preceded by the Cromerian Stage and succeeded by the Hoxnian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Elsterian Stage of NW Europe, and with Marine Isotope Stage 12 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Anisian Age is a division of geological time within the Triassic Period. It is the first of the two ages within the Mid Triassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Olenekian Age (Early Triassic Epoch) and succeeded by the Ladinian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 25.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Antian/Bramertonian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a temporate (interglacial) interval. It is preceded by the Thurnian Stage and succeeded by the Pre-Pastonian/Baventian Stage. It is contemporaneous with Tiglian Substage C1-4b of NW Europe (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Aptian Age is a division of geological time within the Cretaceous Period. It is the fifth of the six ages within the Early Cretaceous Epoch. It is preceded by the Barremian Age and succeeded by the Albian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Aquitanian Age is a division of geological time within the Neogene Period. It is the first of the six ages within the Miocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Chattian Age (Paleogene Period) and succeeded by the Burdigalian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 29.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Archean Eon is the second of the three major intervals of Precambrian time. It is preceded by the Hadean, and succeeded by the Proterozoic Eon (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Arenig Series is the second of five series in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the Tremadoc Series and succeeded by the Llanvirn Series (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Arnsbergian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of seven substages of the Namurian Stage. It is preceded by the Pendleian Substage and succeeded by the Chokierian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Artinskian Age is a division of geological time within the Permian Period. It is the third of the four ages within the Cisuralian Epoch. It is preceded by the Sakmarian Age and succeeded by the Kungurian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Arundian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of five substages of the Visean Stage. It is preceded by the Chadian Substage and succeeded by the Holkerian Substage (BGS Research Report RR/10/07, table 1).

Asbian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the fourth of five substages of the Visean Stage. It is preceded by the Holkerian Substage and succeeded by the Brigantian Substage (BGS Research Report RR/10/07, table 1).
Ashgill Series is the last of five series in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the Caradoc Series (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Asselian Age is a division of geological time within the Permian Period. It is the first of the four ages within the Cisuralian Epoch. It is preceded by the Gzhelian Age (Carboniferous Period) and succeeded by the Sakmarian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Asturian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the last of four substages of the Westphalian Stage. It is preceded by the Bolsovian Substage and succeeded by the Cantabrian Substage (Stephanian Stage) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5). Replaces: Westphalian Substage D.

Aurelucian Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of four stages of the Caradoc Series. It is preceded by the Llandeilian Stage (Llanvirn Series) and succeeded by the Burrellian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Autunian Stage is the last of six stages of the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme, and extends into the Permian Period. It is preceded by the Stephanian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5, 24.9).

Bajocian Age is a division of geological time within the Jurassic Period. It is the second of the four ages within the Mid Jurassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Aalenian Age and succeeded by the Bathonian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Barremian Age is a division of geological time within the Cretaceous Period. It is the fourth of the six ages within the Early Cretaceous Epoch. It is preceded by the Hauterivian Age and succeeded by the Aptian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Bartonian Age is a division of geological time within the Paleogene Period. It is the third of the four ages within the Eocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Lutetian Age and succeeded by the Priabonian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Bashkirian Age is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the only age within the Early Pennsylvanian Epoch. It is preceded by the Serpukhovian Age (Late Mississippian Epoch) and succeeded by the Moscovian Age (Mid Pennsylvanian Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Bathonian Age is a division of geological time within the Jurassic Period. It is the third of the four ages within the Mid Jurassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Bajocian Age and succeeded by the Callovian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Bavelian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the Menapian Stage and succeeded by the Cromerian Complex. It is contemporaneous with the latest part of the Beestonian Stage in Great Britain (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).
Baventian Stage is a deprecated term, replaced by Pre-Pastonian/Baventian Stage (BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Beestonian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a cold (glacial) interval. It is preceded by the Pastonian Stage and succeeded by the Cromerian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Eburonian to Bavelian stages of NW Europe (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b). It is named for the village of Beeston, Norfolk, England.

Berriasian Age is a division of geological time within the Cretaceous Period. It is the first of the six ages within the Early Cretaceous Epoch. It is preceded by the Tithonian Age (Jurassic Period) and succeeded by the Valanginian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Bolsovian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the third of four substages of the Westphalian Stage. It is preceded by the Duckmantian Substage and succeeded by the Asturian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5). Replaces: Westphalian Substage C.

Brigantian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the last of five substages of the Visean Stage. It is preceded by the Asbian Substage and succeeded by the Pendleian Substage (Namurian Stage) (BGS Research Report RR/10/07, table 1).

Burdigalian Age is a division of geological time within the Neogene Period. It is the second of the six ages within the Miocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Aquitanian Age and succeeded by the Langhian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 29.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Burrellian Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of four stages of the Caradoc Series. It is preceded by the Aurelucian Stage and succeeded by the Cheneyan Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Calabrian Age is a division of geological time within the Quaternary Period. It is the second of the four ages within the Pleistocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Gelasian Age and succeeded by the Chibanian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 30.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Callovian Age is a division of geological time within the Jurassic Period. It is the last of the four ages within the Mid Jurassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Bathonian Age and succeeded by the Oxfordian Age (Late Jurassic Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Calymmian Period is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the first of the three periods of the Mesoproterozoic Era. It is preceded by the Stratherian Period (Paleoproterozoic Era) and succeeded by the Ectasian Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Cambrian Period is the first of the six periods of the Palaeozoic Era. It is preceded by the Ediacaran Period (Neoproterozoic Era) and succeeded by the Ordovician Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Cambrian Series 2 is the second of the four epochs of the Cambrian Period. It is preceded by the Terreneuvian Epoch and succeeded by the Miaolingian Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Cambrian Stage 10 is a division of geological time within the Cambrian Period. It is the last of the three ages within the Furongian Epoch. It is preceded by the Jiangshanian Age and succeeded by the Tremadocian Age (Ordovician Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Cambrian Stage 2 is a division of geological time within the Cambrian Period. It is the second of the two ages of the Terreneuvian Epoch. It is preceded by the Fortunian Age and succeeded by Cambrian Stage 3 (of Cambrian Series 2) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Cambrian Stage 3 is a division of geological time within the Cambrian Period. It is the first of the two ages within Cambrian Series 2. It is preceded by Cambrian Stage 2 (Terreneuvian Epoch) and succeeded by Cambrian Stage 4 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Cambrian Stage 4 is a division of geological time within the Cambrian Period. It is the second of the two ages within Cambrian Series 2. It is preceded by Cambrian Stage 3 and succeeded by the Wuliuan Age (of the Miaolingian Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Campanian Age is a division of geological time within the Cretaceous Period. It is the fifth of the six ages within the Late Cretaceous Epoch. It is preceded by the Santonian Age and succeeded by the Maastrichtian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Cantabrian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of four substages of the Stephanian Stage. It is preceded by the Asturian Substage (Westphalian Stage) and succeeded by Stephanian Substage A (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Capitanian Age is a division of geological time within the Permian Period. It is the last of the three ages within the Guadalupian Epoch. It is preceded by the Wordian Age and succeeded by the Wuchiapingian Age (Lopingian Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Caradoc Series is the fourth of five series in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the Llanvirn Series and succeeded by the Ashgill Series (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Prior to revision of the Ordovician series and stages in the type area of England and Wales by Fortey et al. (1995), the base of the Caradoc Series was considered to be at a much higher stratigraphic level, approximating to the base of the Costonian Stage. This is now a deprecated definition of the Caradoc Series, approximately equating to the modern Costonian Substage - Onnian Substage interval (Fortey et al., 1995, fig. 1).

Carboniferous Period is the fifth of the six periods of the Paleozoic Era. It is preceded by the Devonian Period and succeeded by the Permian Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Carnian Age is a division of geological time within the Triassic Period. It is the first of the three ages within the Late Triassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Ladinian Age (Mid Triassic Epoch) and succeeded by the Norian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 25.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Cautleyan Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of four stages of the Ashgill Series. It is preceded by the Pusgillian Stage and succeeded by the Rawtheyan Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Cenomanian Age is a division of geological time within the Cretaceous Period. It is the first of the six ages within the Late Cretaceous Epoch. It is preceded by the Albian Age (Early Cretaceous Epoch) and succeeded by the Turonian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Cenozoic Era is the last of the three eras of the Phanerozoic Eon. It includes the Paleogene, Neogene and Quaternary periods. It is the era in which we live. It is preceded by the Mesozoic Era (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Chadian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of five substages of the Visean Stage. It is preceded by the Courceyan Substage (Tournaisian Stage) and succeeded by the Arundian Substage (BGS Research Report RR/10/07, table 1).

Changhsingian Age is a division of geological time within the Permian Period. It is the second of the two ages within the Lopingian Epoch. It is preceded by the Wuchiapingian Age and succeeded by the Induan Age (Triassic Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Chattian Age is a division of geological time within the Paleogene Period. It is the second of the two ages within the Oligocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Rupelian Age and succeeded by the Aquitanian Age (Neogene Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Cheneyan Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the third of four stages of the Caradoc Series. It is preceded by the Burrellian Stage and succeeded by the Streffordian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Chibanian Age is a division of geological time within the Quaternary Period. It is the third of the four ages within the Pleistocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Calabrian Age and succeeded by the Upper Pleistocene Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 30.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/). Replaces: Ionian Age.

Chokierian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the third of seven substages of the Namurian Stage. It is preceded by the Arnsbergian Substage and succeeded by the Alportian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Cisuralian Epoch is the first of the three epochs of the Permian Period. It is preceded by the Late Pennsylvanian Epoch (Carboniferous Period) and succeeded by the Guadalupian Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/). Replaces: Early Permian Epoch.
Comley Series is the first of three series in the British regional Cambrian stratigraphic scheme. It is succeeded by the St David's Series.

Coniacian Age is a division of geological time within the Cretaceous Period. It is the third of the six ages within the Late Cretaceous Epoch. It is preceded by the Turonian Age and succeeded by the Santonian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Costonian Substage is a substage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of two substages of the Aurelucian Stage. It is preceded by the Velfreyan Substage and succeeded by the Harnagian Substage (Burrellian Stage) (BGS Research Report RR/12/04, table 1).

Courceyan Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the only substage of the Tournaisian Stage. It is succeeded by the Chadian Substage (Visean Stage) (BGS Research Report RR/10/07, table 1).

Cressagian Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of two stages of the Tremadoc Series. It is succeeded by the Migneintian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Cretaceous Period is the third of the three periods of the Mesozoic Era. It is preceded by the Jurassic Period and succeeded by the Paleogene Period (Cenozoic Era) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Cromerian Complex is an Early-to-Mid Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a temporate (interglacial) interval. It is preceded by the Bavelian Stage and succeeded by the Elsterian Stage. It is contemporanerous with the Cromerian Stage in Great Britain, and with marine isotope stages 13-21 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Cromerian Stage is an Early-to-Mid Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a temporate (interglacial) interval. It is preceded by the Beestonian Stage and succeeded by the Anglian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Cromerian Complex of NW Europe, and with marine isotope stages 13-21 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Cryogenian Period is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the second of the three periods of the Neoproterozoic Era. It is preceded by the Tonian Period and succeeded by the Ediacaran Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Danian Age is a division of geological time within the Paleogene Period. It is the first of the three ages within the Paleocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Maastrichtian Age (Cretaceous Period) and succeeded by the Selandian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Dapingian Age is a division of geological time within the Ordovician Period. It is the first of the two ages within the Mid Ordovician Epoch. It is preceded by the Floian Age (Early Ordovician Epoch) and succeeded by the Darriwilian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 20.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Darriwilian Age is a division of geological time within the Ordovician Period. It is the second of the two ages within the Mid Ordovician Epoch. It is preceded by the Dapingian Age and succeeded by the Sandbian Age (Late Ordovician Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 20.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Devensian Stage is the last Late Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a cold (glacial) interval. It is preceded by the Ipswichian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Weichselian Stage in NW Europe (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Devonian Period is the fourth of the six periods of the Paleozoic Era. It is preceded by the Silurian Period and succeeded by the Carboniferous Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 22.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Dimlington Stadial is a relatively cold period near the end of the Devensian Stage. It is succeeded by the Windermere Interstadial (BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b; BGS British Regional Geology: Northern England (Fifth edition), fig. 64).

Dinantian Subsystem is a deprecated European term for the Lower Carboniferous, approximately equating to the Early Mississippian Epoch - Mid Mississippian Epoch interval (Geologic Time Scale 2020, chapter 23; BGS Research Report RR/10/007, table 1).

Drumian Age is a division of geological time within the Cambrian Period. It is the second of the three ages within the Miaolingian Epoch. It is preceded by the Wuliuan Age and succeeded by the Guzhangian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Duckmantian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of four substages of the Westphalian Stage. It is preceded by the Langsettian Substage and succeeded by the Bolsovian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5). Replaces: Westphalian Substage B.

Early Cretaceous Epoch is the first of the two epochs of the Cretaceous Period. It is preceded by the Late Jurassic Epoch (Jurassic Period) and succeeded by the Late Cretaceous Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Early Devonian Epoch is the first of the three epochs of the Devonian Period. It is preceded by the Pridoli Epoch (Silurian Period) and succeeded by the Mid Devonian Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 22.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Early Eocene is the first of three informal subdivisions of the Eocene Epoch. It equates to the Ypresian Age of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Early Jurassic Epoch is the first of the three epochs of the Jurassic Period. It is preceded by the Late Triassic Epoch (Triassic Period) and succeeded by the Mid Jurassic Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Early Miocene is the first of three informal subdivisions of the Miocene Epoch. It equates to the Aquitanian plus Burdigalian ages of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Early Mississippian Epoch is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the first of the three epochs within the Mississippian Subperiod. It is preceded by the Late Devonian Epoch (Devonian Period) and succeeded by the Mid Mississippian Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Early Oligocene is the first of two informal subdivisions of the Oligocene Epoch. It equates to the Rupelian Age of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Early Ordovician Epoch is the first of the three epochs of the Ordovician Period. It is preceded by the Furongian Epoch (Cambrian Period) and succeeded by the Mid Ordovician Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 20.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Early Paleocene is the first of three informal subdivisions of the Paleocene Epoch. It equates to the Danian Age of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.
Early Paleozoic is the first of two informal subdivisions of the Paleozoic Era. It includes the Cambrian, Ordovician and Silurian periods of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Early Pennsylvanian Epoch is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the first of the three epochs within the Pennsylvanian Subperiod. It is preceded by the Late Mississippian Epoch (Mississippian Subperiod) and succeeded by the Mid Pennsylvanian Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Early Permian is a deprecated term, replaced by Cisuralian Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 1.4).

Early Pleistocene is the first of three informal subdivisions of the Pleistocene Epoch. It equates to the Gelasian plus Calabrian ages of the international standard stratigraphic scheme (BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).
Early Pliocene is the first of two informal subdivisions of the Pliocene Epoch. It equates to the Zanclean Age of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Early Triassic Epoch is the first of the three epochs of the Triassic Period. It is preceded by the Lopingian Epoch (Permian Period) and succeeded by the Mid Triassic Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 25.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/). Replaces: Scythian Age.

Eburonian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a cold (glacial) interval. It is preceded by the Tiglian Stage and succeeded by the Waalian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the early part of the Beestonian Stage in Great Britain (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Ectasian Period is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the second of the three periods of the Mesoproterozoic Era. It is preceded by the Calymmian Period and succeeded by the Stenian Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Ediacaran Period is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the last of the three periods of the Neoproterozoic Era. It is preceded by the Cryogenian Period and succeeded by the Cambrian Period (Paleozoic Era) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/). Replaces: Neoproterozoic Period III.

Eemian Stage is a Late Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a temporate (interglacial) interval. It is preceded by the Saalian Stage and succeeded by the Weichselian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Ipswichian Stage in Great Britain, and with Marine Isotope Stage 5e (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Eifelian Age is a division of geological time within the Devonian Period. It is the first of the two ages within the Mid Devonian Epoch. It is preceded by the Emsian Age (Early Devonian Epoch) and succeeded by the Givetian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 22.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Elsterian Stage is a Mid Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a cold (glacial) interval. It is preceded by the Cromerian Complex and succeeded by the Holsteinian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Anglian Stage in Great Britain, and with Marine Isotope Stage 12 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Emsian Age is a division of geological time within the Devonian Period. It is the last of the three ages within the Early Devonian Epoch. It is preceded by the Pragian Age and succeeded by the Eifelian Age (Mid Devonian Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 22.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Eoarchean Era is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the first of the four eras of the Archean Eon. It is preceded by the Hadean and succeeded by the Paleoarchean Era (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Eocene Epoch is the second of the three epochs of the Paleogene Period. It is preceded by the Paleocene Epoch and succeeded by the Oligocene Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Famennian Age is a division of geological time within the Devonian Period. It is the second of the two ages within the Late Devonian Epoch. It is preceded by the Frasnian Age and succeeded by the Early Mississippian Epoch (Carboniferous Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 22.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Fennian Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the last of three stages of the Arenig Series. It is preceded by the Whitlandian Stage and succeeded by the Abereiddian Stage (Llanvirn Series) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).
Flandrian Age is a deprecated term, replaced by Holocene Epoch (Geologic time Scale 2020, chapter 30).

Floian Age is a division of geological time within the Ordovician Period. It is the second of the two ages within the Early Ordovician Epoch. It is preceded by the Tremadocian Age and succeeded by the Dapingian Age (Mid Ordovician Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 20.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Fortunian Age is a division of geological time within the Cambrian Period. It is the first of the two ages of the Terreneuvian Epoch. It is preceded by the Ediacaran Period (Precambrian) and succeeded by Cambrian Stage 2 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Frasnian Age is a division of geological time within the Devonian Period. It is the first of the two ages within the Late Devonian Epoch. It is preceded by the Givetian Age (Mid Devonian Epoch) and succeeded by the Famennian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 22.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Furongian Epoch is the last of the four epochs of the Cambrian Period. It is preceded by the Miaolingian Epoch and succeeded by the Early Ordovician Epoch (Ordovician Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Gelasian Age is a division of geological time within the Quaternary Period. It is the first of the four ages within the Pleistocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Piacenzian Age (Neogene Period) and succeeded by the Calabrian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 30.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Geological Time (root of geochronological classification).

Givetian Age is a division of geological time within the Devonian Period. It is the second of the two ages within the Mid Devonian Epoch. It is preceded by the Eifelian Age and succeeded by the Frasnian Age (Late Devonian Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 22.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Gorstian Age is a division of geological time within the Silurian Period. It is the first of the two ages within the Ludlow Epoch. It is preceded by the Homerian Age (Wenlock Epoch) and succeeded by the Ludfordian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 21.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Greenlandian Age is a division of geological time within the Quaternary Period. It is the first of three ages within the Holocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Upper Pleistocene Age (Pleistocene Epoch) and succeeded by the Northgrippian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 30.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Guadalupian Epoch is the second of the three epochs of the Permian Period. It is preceded by the Cisuralian Epoch and succeeded by the Lopingian Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Guzhangian Age is a division of geological time within the Cambrian Period. It is the last of the three ages within the Miaolingian Epoch. It is preceded by the Drumian Age and succeeded by the Paibian Age (Furongian Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Gzhelian Age is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the second of the two ages within the Late Pennsylvanian Epoch. It is preceded by the Kasimovian Age and succeeded by the Asselian Age (Permian Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Hadean is an informal name for the first of the three major intervals of Precambrian time. It is succeeded by the Archean Eon (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Harnagian Substage is a substage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of three substages of the Burrellian Stage. It is preceded by the Costonian Substage (Aurelucian Stage) and succeeded by the Soudleyan Substage (BGS Research Report RR/12/04, table 1).

Hauterivian Age is a division of geological time within the Cretaceous Period. It is the third of the six ages within the Early Cretaceous Epoch. It is preceded by the Valanginian Age and succeeded by the Barremian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Hettangian Age is a division of geological time within the Jurassic Period. It is the first of the four ages within the Early Jurassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Rhaetian Age (Triassic Period) and succeeded by the Sinemurian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Hirnantian Age is a division of geological time within the Ordovician Period. It is the last of the three ages within the Late Ordovician Epoch. It is preceded by the Katian Age and succeeded by the Rhuddanian Age (Silurian Period). The Hirnantian Stage is also the last of four stages in the Ashgill Series in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the Rawtheyan Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 20.1, 20.12; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Holkerian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the third of five substages of the Visean Stage. It is preceded by the Arundian Substage and succeeded by the Asbian Substage (BGS Research Report RR/10/07, table 1).

Holocene Epoch is the second of the two epochs of the Quaternary Period. It is the epoch in which we live. It is preceded by the Pleistocene Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 30.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/). Replaces: Flandrian Age.

Holsteinian Stage is a Mid Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a temporate (interglacial) interval. It is preceded by the Elsterian Stage and succeeded by the Saalian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Hoxnian Stage in Great Britain, and with Marine Isotope Stage 11 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Homerian Age is a division of geological time within the Silurian Period. It is the second of the two ages within the Wenlock Epoch. It is preceded by the Sheinwoodian Age and succeeded by the Gorstian Age (Ludlow Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 21.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Hoxnian Stage is a Mid Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a temporate (interglacial) interval. It is preceded by the Anglian Stage and succeeded by the Wolstonian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Holsteinian Stage of NW Europe, and with Marine Isotope Stage 11 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b). It is named for the village of Hoxne, Suffolk, England.

Induan Age is a division of geological time within the Triassic Period. It is the first of the two ages within the Early Triassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Changhsingian Age (Permian Period) and succeeded by the Olenekian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 25.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Ipswichian Stage is a Late Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a temporate (interglacial) interval. It is preceded by the Wolstonian Stage and succeeded by the Devensian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Eemian Stage of NW Europe, and with Marine Isotope Stage 5e (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b). It is named for the town of Ipswich, Suffolk, England.

Jiangshanian Age is a division of geological time within the Cambrian Period. It is the second of the three ages within the Furongian Epoch. It is preceded by the Paibian Age and succeeded by Cambrian Stage 10 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Jurassic Period is the second of the three periods of the Mesozoic Era. It is preceded by the Triassic Period and succeeded by the Cretaceous Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Kasimovian Age is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the first of the two ages within the Late Pennsylvanian Epoch. It is preceded by the Moscovian Age (Mid Pennsylvanian Epoch) and succeeded by the Gzhelian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Katian Age is a division of geological time within the Ordovician Period. It is the second of the three ages within the Late Ordovician Epoch. It is preceded by the Sandbian Age and succeeded by the Hirnantian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 20.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Kimmeridgian Age is a division of geological time within the Jurassic Period. It is the second of the three ages within the Late Jurassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Oxfordian Age and succeeded by the Tithonian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Kinderscoutian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the fifth of seven substages of the Namurian Stage. It is preceded by the Alportian Substage and succeeded by the Marsdenian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Kungurian Age is a division of geological time within the Permian Period. It is the last of the four ages within the Cisuralian Epoch. It is preceded by the Artinskian Age and succeeded by the Roadian Age (Guadalupian Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Ladinian Age is a division of geological time within the Triassic Period. It is the second of the two ages within the Mid Triassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Anisian Age and succeeded by the Carnian Age (Late Triassic Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 25.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Langhian Age is a division of geological time within the Neogene Period. It is the third of the six ages within the Miocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Burdigalian Age and succeeded by the Serravallian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 29.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Langsettian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of four substages of the Westphalian Stage. It is preceded by the Yeadonian Substage (Namurian Stage) and succeeded by the Duckmantian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5). Replaces: Westphalian Substage A.

Late Cretaceous Epoch is the second of the two epochs of the Cretaceous Period. It is preceded by the Early Cretaceous Epoch and succeeded by the Paleocene Epoch (Paleogene Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Late Devonian Epoch is the last of the three epochs of the Devonian Period. It is preceded by the Mid Devonian Epoch and succeeded by the Early Mississippian Epoch (Carboniferous Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 22.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Late Eocene is the last of three informal subdivisions of the Eocene Epoch. It equates to the Priabonian Age of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Late Jurassic Epoch is the last of the three epochs of the Jurassic Period. It is preceded by the Mid Jurassic Epoch and succeeded by the Early Cretaceous Epoch (Cretaceous Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Late Miocene is the last of three informal subdivisions of the Miocene Epoch. It equates to the Tortonian plus Messinian ages of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Late Mississippian Epoch is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the last of the three epochs within the Mississippian Subperiod. It is preceded by the Mid Mississippian Epoch and succeeded by the Early Pennsylvanian Epoch (Pennsylvanian Subperiod) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Late Oligocene is the second of two informal subdivisions of the Oligocene Epoch. It equates to the Chattian Age of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Late Ordovician Epoch is the last of the three epochs of the Ordovician Period. It is preceded by the Mid Ordovician Epoch and succeeded by the Llandovery Epoch (Silurian Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 20.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Late Paleocene is the last of three informal subdivisions of the Paleocene Epoch. It equates to the Thanetian Age of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.
Late Paleozoic is the second of two informal subdivisions of the Paleozoic Era. It includes the Devonian, Carboniferous and Permian periods of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Late Pennsylvanian Epoch is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the last of the three epochs within the Pennsylvanian Subperiod. It is preceded by the Mid Pennsylvanian Epoch and succeeded by the Cisuralian Epoch (Permian Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Late Permian is a deprecated term, equating to the Guadalupian Epoch - Lopingian Epoch interval (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 1.4).

Late Pleistocene is the last of three informal subdivisions of the Pleistocene Epoch. It equates to the Upper Pleistocene Age of the international standard stratigraphic scheme (BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).
Late Pliocene is the second of two informal subdivisions of the Pliocene Epoch. It equates to the Piacenzian Age of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Late Triassic Epoch is the last of the three epochs of the Triassic Period. It is preceded by the Mid Triassic Epoch and succeeded by the Early Jurassic Epoch (Jurassic Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 25.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Llandeilian Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of two stages of the Llanvirn Series. It is preceded by the Abereiddian Stage and succeeded by the Aurelucian Stage (Caradoc Series) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).
Llandeilo Series is a deprecated term, a British regional Ordovician series approximately equating to the modern Llandeilian Stage - Velfreyan Substage interval (Fortey et al., 1995, fig. 1).

Llandovery Epoch is the first of the four epochs of the Silurian Period. It is preceded by the Late Ordovician Epoch (Ordovician Period) and succeeded by the Wenlock Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 21.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Llanvirn Series is the third of five series in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the Arenig Series and succeeded by the Caradoc Series (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Prior to revision of the Ordovician series and stages in the type area of England and Wales by Fortey et al. (1995), the top of the Llanvirn Series was considered to be at a lower stratigraphic level, approximating to the top of the modern Abereiddian Stage. This is now a deprecated definition of the Llanvirn Series, approximately equating to the modern Abereiddian Stage (Fortey et al., 1995, fig. 1).

Loch Lomond Stadial is a relatively cold period near the end of the Devensian Stage. It is preceded by the Windermere Interstadial (BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b; BGS British Regional Geology: Northern England (Fifth edition), fig. 64).

Lochkovian Age is a division of geological time within the Devonian Period. It is the first of the three ages within the Early Devonian Epoch. It is preceded by the Pridoli Epoch (Silurian Period) and succeeded by the Pragian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 22.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Longvillian Substage is a substage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the last of three substages of the Burrellian Stage. It is preceded by the Soudleyan Substage and succeeded by the Woolstonian Substage (Cheneyan Stage) (BGS Research Report RR/12/04, table 1).

Lopingian Epoch is the last of the three epochs of the Permian Period. It is preceded by the Guadalupian Epoch and succeeded by the Early Triassic Epoch (Triassic Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Ludfordian Age is a division of geological time within the Silurian Period. It is the second of the two ages within the Ludlow Epoch. It is preceded by the Gorstian Age and succeeded by the Pridoli Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 21.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Ludhamian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a temporate (interglacial) interval. It is preceded by the Pre-Ludhamian Stage and succeeded by the Thurnian Stage. It is contemporaneous with Tiglian Substage A of NW Europe (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b). It is named for the town of Ludham, England.

Ludlow Epoch is the third of the four epochs of the Silurian Period. It is preceded by the Wenlock Epoch and succeeded by the Pridoli Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 21.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Lutetian Age is a division of geological time within the Paleogene Period. It is the second of the four ages within the Eocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Ypresian Age and succeeded by the Bartonian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Maastrichtian Age is a division of geological time within the Cretaceous Period. It is the last of the six ages within the Late Cretaceous Epoch. It is preceded by the Campanian Age and succeeded by the Danian Age (Paleogene Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
