Marsdenian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the sixth of seven substages of the Namurian Stage. It is preceded by the Kinderscoutian Substage and succeeded by the Yeadonian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Marshbrookian Substage is a substage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of two substages of the Cheneyan Stage. It is preceded by the Woolstonian Substage and succeeded by the Actonian Substage (Streffordian Stage) (BGS Research Report RR/12/04, table 1).

Meghalayan Age is a division of geological time within the Quaternary Period. It is the last of three ages within the Holocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Northgrippian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 30.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Menapian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a cold (glacial) interval. It is preceded by the Waalian Stage and succeeded by the Bavelian Stage. It is contemporaneous with part of the Beestonian Stage in Great Britain (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).
Merioneth Series is the last of three series in the British regional Cambrian stratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the St David's Series.

Mesoarchean Era is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the third of the four eras of the Archean Eon. It is preceded by the Paleoarchean Era and succeeded by the Neoarchean Era (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Mesoproterozoic Era is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the second of the three eras of the Proterozoic Eon. It is preceded by the Paleoproterozoic Era and succeeded by the Neoproterozoic Era (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Mesozoic Era is the second of the three eras of the Phanerozoic Eon. It includes the Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous periods. It is preceded by the Paleozoic Era and succeeded by the Cenozoic Era (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Messinian Age is a division of geological time within the Neogene Period. It is the last of the six ages within the Miocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Tortonian Age and succeeded by the Zanclean Age (Pliocene Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 29.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Miaolingian Epoch is the third of the four epochs of the Cambrian Period. It is preceded by Cambrian Series 2 and succeeded by the Furongian Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Mid Devonian Epoch is the second of the three epochs of the Devonian Period. It is preceded by the Early Devonian Epoch and succeeded by the Late Devonian Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 22.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Mid Eocene is the second of three informal subdivisions of the Eocene Epoch. It equates to the Lutetian plus Bartonian ages of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Mid Jurassic Epoch is the second of the three epochs of the Jurassic Period. It is preceded by the Early Jurassic Epoch and succeeded by the Late Jurassic Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Mid Miocene is the second of three informal subdivisions of the Miocene Epoch. It equates to the Langhian plus Serravallian ages of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Mid Mississippian Epoch is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the second of the three epochs within the Mississippian Subperiod. It is preceded by the Early Mississippian Epoch and succeeded by the Late Mississippian Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Mid Ordovician Epoch is the second of the three epochs of the Ordovician Period. It is preceded by the Early Ordovician Epoch and succeeded by the Late Ordovician Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 20.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Mid Paleocene is the second of three informal subdivisions of the Paleocene Epoch. It equates to the Selandian Age of the international standard stratigraphic scheme.

Mid Pennsylvanian Epoch is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the second of the three epochs within the Pennsylvanian Subperiod. It is preceded by the Early Pennsylvanian Epoch and succeeded by the Late Pennsylvanian Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Mid Pleistocene is the second of three informal subdivisions of the Pleistocene Epoch. It equates to the Chibanian Age of the international standard stratigraphic scheme (BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Mid Triassic Epoch is the second of the three epochs of the Triassic Period. It is preceded by the Early Triassic Epoch and succeeded by the Late Triassic Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 25.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Migneintian Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of two stages of the Tremadoc Series. It is preceded by the Cressagian Stage and succeeded by the Moridunian Stage (Arenig Series) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Miocene Epoch is the first of the two epochs of the Neogene Period. It is preceded by the Oligocene Epoch (Paleogene Period) and succeeded by the Pliocene Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 29.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Mississippian Subperiod is the first of two major subdivisions of the Carboniferous Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Moridunian Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of three stages of the Arenig Series. It is preceded by the Migneintian Stage (Tremadoc Series) and succeeded by the Whitlandian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Moscovian Age is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the only age within the Mid Pennsylvanian Epoch. It is preceded by the Bashkirian Age (Early Pennsylvanian Epoch) and succeeded by the Kasimovian Age (Late Pennsylvanian Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Namurian Stage is the third of six stages of the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the Visean Stage and succeeded by the Westphalian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Neoarchean Era is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the last of the four eras of the Archean Eon. It is preceded by the Mesoarchean Era and succeeded by the Paleoproterozoic Era (Proterozoic Eon) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Neogene Period is the second of the three periods of the Cenozoic Era. It is preceded by the Paleogene Period and succeeded by the Quaternary Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 29.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Prior to the 2009 decision by the International Union of Geological Sciences (IUGS) to place the base of the Quaternary Period at a level coinciding with the base of the Gelasian Age, the Neogene Period was considered to include the Gelasian Age and to have an upper boundary at approximately 1.8 Ma BP. This is now a deprecated definition and equates to the modern Neogene Period - Gelasian Age interval (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.1).

Neoproterozoic Era is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the last of the three eras of the Proterozoic Eon. It is preceded by the Mesoproterozoic Era and succeeded by the Paleozoic Era (Phanerozoic Eon) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Neoproterozoic Period III is a deprecated term, replaced by Ediacaran Period.

Norian Age is a division of geological time within the Triassic Period. It is the second of the three ages within the Late Triassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Carnian Age and succeeded by the Rhaetian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 25.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Northgrippian Age is a division of geological time within the Quaternary Period. It is the second of three ages within the Holocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Greenlandian Age and succeeded by the Meghalayan Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 30.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Olenekian Age is a division of geological time within the Triassic Period. It is the second of the two ages within the Early Triassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Induan Age and succeeded by the Anisian Age (Mid Triassic Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 25.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Oligocene Epoch is the last of the three epochs of the Paleogene Period. It is preceded by the Eocene Epoch and succeeded by the Miocene Epoch (Neogene Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Onnian Substage is a substage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of two substages of the Streffordian Stage. It is preceded by the Actonian Substage and succeeded by the Pusgillian Stage (BGS Research Report RR/12/04, table 1).

Ordovician Period is the second of the six periods of the Paleozoic Era. It is preceded by the Cambrian Period and succeeded by the Silurian Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 20.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Orosirian Period is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the third of the four periods of the Paleoproterozoic Era. It is preceded by the Rhyacian Period and succeeded by the Statherian Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Oxfordian Age is a division of geological time within the Jurassic Period. It is the first of the three ages within the Late Jurassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Callovian Age (Mid Jurassic Epoch) and succeeded by the Kimmeridgian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Paibian Age is a division of geological time within the Cambrian Period. It is the first of the three ages within the Furongian Epoch. It is preceded by the Guzhangian Age (of the Miaolingian Epoch) and succeeded by the Jiangshanian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Paleoarchean Era is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the second of the four eras of the Archean Eon. It is preceded by the Eoarchean Era and succeeded by the Mesoarchean Era (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Paleocene Epoch is the first of the three epochs of the Paleogene Period. It is preceded by the Late Cretaceous Epoch (Cretaceous Period) and succeeded by the Eocene Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Paleogene Period is the first of the three periods of the Cenozoic Era. It is preceded by the Cretaceous Period (Mesozoic Era) and succeeded by the Neogene Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Paleoproterozoic Era is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the first of the three eras of the Proterozoic Eon. It is preceded by the Neoarchean Era (Archean Eon) and succeeded by the Mesoproterozoic Era (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Paleozoic Era is the first of the three eras of the Phanerozoic Eon. It includes the Cambrian, Ordovician, Silurian, Devonian, Carboniferous and Permian periods. It is preceded by the Neoproterozoic Era (Proterozoic Eon) and succeeded by the Mesozoic Era (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Pastonian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a temporate (interglacial) interval. It is preceded by the Pre-Pastonian/Baventian Stage and succeeded by the Beestonian Stage. It is contemporaneous with Tiglian Substage C5-6 of NW Europe (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b). It is named for the village of Paston, Norfolk, England.

Pendleian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of seven substages of the Namurian Stage. It is preceded by the Brigantian Substage (Visean Stage) and succeeded by the Arnsbergian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).
Pennsylvanian Subperiod is the second of two major subdivisions of the Carboniferous Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Permian Period is the last of the six periods of the Paleozoic Era. It is preceded by the Carboniferous Period and succeeded by the Triassic Period (Mesozoic Era) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Phanerozoic Eon is the time interval characterised by deposition of rocks containing abundant evidence of life. It is the eon in which we live. It is preceded by the Proterozoic Eon (Precambrian) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1).

Piacenzian Age is a division of geological time within the Neogene Period. It is the second of the two ages within the Pliocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Zanclean Age and succeeded by the Gelasian Age (Quaternary Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 29.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/). Replaces: Waltonian Age.

Prior to the 2009 decision by the International Union of Geological Sciences (IUGS) to place the base of the Quaternary Period at a level coinciding with the base of the Gelasian Age, the Piacenzian Age was considered to have an upper boundary at approximately 1.8 Ma BP. This is now a deprecated definition and equates to the modern Piacenzian Age - Gelasian Age interval (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.1).

Pleistocene Epoch is the first of the two epochs of the Quaternary Period. It is preceded by the Pliocene Epoch (Neogene Period) and succeeded by the Holocene Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 30.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Prior to the 2009 decision by the International Union of Geological Sciences (IUGS) to place the base of the Quaternary Period at a level coinciding with the base of the Gelasian Age, the Pleistocene Epoch was considered not to include the Gelasian Age and to have a lower boundary at approximately 1.8 Ma BP. This is now a deprecated definition and equates to the modern Calabrian Age - Tarantian Age interval (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.1).

Pliensbachian Age is a division of geological time within the Jurassic Period. It is the third of the four ages within the Early Jurassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Sinemurian Age and succeeded by the Toarcian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Pliocene Epoch is the second of the two epochs of the Neogene Period. It is preceded by the Miocene Epoch and succeeded by the Pleistocene Epoch (Quaternary Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 29.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Prior to the 2009 decision by the International Union of Geological Sciences (IUGS) to place the base of the Quaternary Period at a level coinciding with the base of the Gelasian Age, the Pliocene Epoch was considered to include the Gelasian Age and to have an upper boundary at approximately 1.8 Ma BP. This is now a deprecated definition and equates to the modern Pliocene Epoch - Gelasian Age interval (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.1).

Portlandian Stage is a deprecated term, a British regional stage approximately equating to the late Tithonian Age (Jurassic Period) - earliest Berriasian Age (Cretaceous Period) interval (Geologic Time Scale 2012, fig. 26.8).

Praetiglian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the Reuverian Stage and succeeded by the Tiglian Stage. It is contemporaneous with marine isotope stages 96-100 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Pragian Age is a division of geological time within the Devonian Period. It is the second of the three ages within the Early Devonian Epoch. It is preceded by the Lochkovian Age and succeeded by the Emsian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 22.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Pre-Ludhamian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is succeeded by the Ludhamian Stage. It is contemporaneous with Marine Isotope Stage 96 and greater (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Pre-Pastonian/Baventian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a cold (glacial) interval. It is preceded by the Antian/Bramertonian Stage and succeeded by the Pastonian Stage. It is contemporaneous with Tiglian Substage C4c of NW Europe (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b). Replaces: Baventian Stage.
Precambrian is an informal name used for the long interval of geological time preceding the Cambrian Period.
Present Day.

Priabonian Age is a division of geological time within the Paleogene Period. It is the last of the four ages within the Eocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Bartonian Age and succeeded by the Rupelian Age (Oligocene Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Pridoli Epoch is the last of the four epochs of the Silurian Period. It is preceded by the Ludlow Epoch and succeeded by the Early Devonian Epoch (Devonian Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 21.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Proterozoic Eon is the last of the three major intervals of Precambrian time. It is preceded by the Archean Eon, and succeeded by the Phanerozoic Eon (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Pusgillian Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of four stages of the Ashgill Series. It is preceded by the Streffordian Stage (Caradoc Series) and succeeded by the Cautleyan Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Quaternary Period is the last of the three periods of the Cenozoic Era. It is the period in which we live. It is preceded by the Neogene Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 30.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Prior to the 2009 decision by the International Union of Geological Sciences (IUGS) to place the base of the Quaternary Period at a level coinciding with the base of the Gelasian Age, the Quaternary Period was considered not to include the Gelasian Age and to have a lower boundary at approximately 1.8 Ma BP. This is now a deprecated definition and equates to the modern Calabrian Age - Holocene Epoch interval (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.1).

Rawtheyan Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the third of four stages of the Ashgill Series. It is preceded by the Cautleyan Stage and succeeded by the Hirnantian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Reuverian Stage is a Pliocene-Early Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a temporate interval. It is succeeded by the Praetiglian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).
Reuverian Substage C is an Early Pleistocene substage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is succeeded by the Praetiglian Stage (BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Rhaetian Age is a division of geological time within the Triassic Period. It is the last of the three ages within the Late Triassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Norian Age and succeeded by the Hettangian Age (Jurassic Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 25.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Rhuddanian Age is a division of geological time within the Silurian Period. It is the first of the three ages within the Llandovery Epoch. It is preceded by the Hirnantian Age (Ordovician Period) and succeeded by the Aeronian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 21.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Rhyacian Period is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the second of the four periods of the Paleoproterozoic Era. It is preceded by the Siderian Period and succeeded by the Orosirian Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Roadian Age is a division of geological time within the Permian Period. It is the first of the three ages within the Guadalupian Epoch. It is preceded by the Kungurian Age (Cisuralian Epoch) and succeeded by the Wordian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Rupelian Age is a division of geological time within the Paleogene Period. It is the first of the two ages within the Oligocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Priabonian Age (Eocene Epoch) and succeeded by the Chattian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Ryazanian Stage is a deprecated term, a British Cretaceous regional stage approximately equating to the Berriasian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 26.9).

Saalian Stage is a Mid Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a cold (glacial) interval. It is preceded by the Holsteinian Stage and succeeded by the Eemian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Wolstonian Stage in Great Britain, and with marine isotope stages 6-10 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Sakmarian Age is a division of geological time within the Permian Period. It is the second of the four ages within the Cisuralian Epoch. It is preceded by the Asselian Age and succeeded by the Artinskian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Sandbian Age is a division of geological time within the Ordovician Period. It is the first of the three ages within the Late Ordovician Epoch. It is preceded by the Darriwilian Age (Mid Ordovician Epoch) and succeeded by the Katian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 20.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Santonian Age is a division of geological time within the Cretaceous Period. It is the fourth of the six ages within the Late Cretaceous Epoch. It is preceded by the Coniacian Age and succeeded by the Campanian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Scythian Age is a deprecated term, replaced by Early Triassic Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 1.5).

Selandian Age is a division of geological time within the Paleogene Period. It is the second of the three ages within the Paleocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Danian Age and succeeded by the Thanetian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Serpukhovian Age is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the only age within the Late Mississippian Epoch. It is preceded by the Visean Age (Mid Mississippian Epoch) and succeeded by the Bashkirian Age (Early Pennsylvanian Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Serravallian Age is a division of geological time within the Neogene Period. It is the fourth of the six ages within the Miocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Langhian Age and succeeded by the Tortonian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 29.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Sheinwoodian Age is a division of geological time within the Silurian Period. It is the first of the two ages within the Wenlock Epoch. It is preceded by the Telychian Age (Llandovery Epoch) and succeeded by the Homerian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 21.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Siderian Period is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the first of the four periods of the Paleoproterozoic Era. It is preceded by the Archean Eon and succeeded by the Rhyacian Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Silesian Subsystem is a deprecated European term for the Upper Carboniferous, approximately equating to the Late Mississippian Epoch - Late Pennsylvanian Epoch interval (Geologic Time Scale 2020, chapter 23; BGS Research Report RR/10/007, table 1).

Silurian Period is the third of the six periods of the Paleozoic Era. It is preceded by the Ordovician Period and succeeded by the Devonian Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 21.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Sinemurian Age is a division of geological time within the Jurassic Period. It is the second of the four ages within the Early Jurassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Hettangian Age and succeeded by the Pliensbachian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Soudleyan Substage is a substage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of three substages of the Burrellian Stage. It is preceded by the Harnagian Substage and succeeded by the Longvillian Substage (BGS Research Report RR/12/04, table 1).
St David's Series is the second of three series in the British regional Cambrian stratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the Comley Series and succeeded by the Merioneth Series.

Statherian Period is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the last of the four periods of the Paleoproterozoic Era. It is preceded by the Orosirian Period and succeeded by the Calymmian Period (Mesoproterozoic Era) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Stenian Period is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the last of the three periods of the Mesoproterozoic Era. It is preceded by the Ectasian Period and succeeded by the Tonian Period (Neoproterozoic Era) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Stephanian Stage is the fifth of six stages of the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the Westphalian Stage and succeeded by the Autunian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Stephanian Substage A is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of four substages of the Stephanian Stage. It is preceded by the Cantabrian Substage and succeeded by Stephanian Substage B (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Stephanian Substage B is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the third of four substages of the Stephanian Stage. It is preceded by Stephanian Substage A and succeeded by Stephanian Substage C (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Stephanian Substage C is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the last of four substages of the Stephanian Stage. It is preceded by Stephanian Substage B and succeeded by the Autunian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Streffordian Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the last of four stages of the Caradoc Series. It is preceded by the Cheneyan Stage and succeeded by the Pusgillian Stage (Ashgill Series) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).
Tatarian Age is a deprecated term, used for Permian rocks on the Russian Platform, approximately equating to the Wordian Age - lower Wuchiapingian Age interval (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 24.9).

Telychian Age is a division of geological time within the Silurian Period. It is the last of the three ages within the Llandovery Epoch. It is preceded by the Aeronian Age and succeeded by the Sheinwoodian Age (Wenlock Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 21.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Terreneuvian Epoch is the first of the four epochs of the Cambrian Period. It is preceded by the Ediacaran Period and succeeded by Cambrian Series 2 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Tertiary is a deprecated term, traditionally used for the interval between the Mesozoic and the Quaternary. It is replaced in modern usage by the Paleogene and Neogene periods (Geologic Time Scale 2012, chapter 28).

Thanetian Age is a division of geological time within the Paleogene Period. It is the last of the three ages within the Paleocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Selandian Age and succeeded by the Ypresian Age (Eocene Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Thurnian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a cold (glacial) interval. It is preceded by the Ludhamian Stage and succeeded by the Antian/Bramertonian Stage. It is contemporaneous with Tiglian Substage B of NW Europe (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Tiglian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the Praetiglian Stage and succeeded by the Eburonian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Ludhamian to Pastonian stages in Great Britain (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Tiglian Substage A is an Early Pleistocene substage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is the first of three substages within the Tiglian Stage. It is succeeded by Tiglian Substage B. It is contemporaneous with the Ludhamian Stage in Great Britain (BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Tiglian Substage B is an Early Pleistocene substage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is the second of three substages within the Tiglian Stage. It is preceded by Tiglian Substage A, and succeeded by Tiglian Substage C. It is contemporaneous with the Thurnian Stage in Great Britain (BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Tiglian Substage C is an Early Pleistocene substage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is the last of three substages within the Tiglian Stage. It is preceded by Tiglian Substage B. It is contemporaneous with the Antian/Bramertonian-to-Pastonian stages in Great Britain (BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Tithonian Age is a division of geological time within the Jurassic Period. It is the last of the three ages within the Late Jurassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Kimmeridgian Age and succeeded by the Berriasian Age (Cretaceous Period) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Toarcian Age is a division of geological time within the Jurassic Period. It is the last of the four ages within the Early Jurassic Epoch. It is preceded by the Pliensbachian Age and succeeded by the Aalenian Age (Mid Jurassic Epoch) (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 26.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Tonian Period is a division of Precambrian geological time. It is the first of the three periods of the Neoproterozoic Era. It is preceded by the Stenian Period (Mesoproterozoic Era) and succeeded by the Cryogenian Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Tortonian Age is a division of geological time within the Neogene Period. It is the fifth of the six ages within the Miocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Serravallian Age and succeeded by the Messinian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 29.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Tournaisian Age is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the only age within the Early Mississippian Epoch. It is preceded by the Famennian Age (Devonian Period) and succeeded by the Visean Age (Mid Mississippian Epoch). The Tournaisian is also the first of six stages comprising the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme, succeeded by the Visean Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.5; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
Tremadoc Series is the first of five series in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is succeeded by the Arenig Series (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).
Deprecated code. Modern usage places the Tremadoc Series in the Ordovician Period (Fortey et al., 1995, fig. 1).

Tremadocian Age is a division of geological time within the Ordovician Period. It is the first of the two ages within the Early Ordovician Epoch. It is preceded by Cambrian Stage 10 (Cambrian Period) and succeeded by the Floian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 20.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Triassic Period is the first of the three periods of the Mesozoic Era. It is preceded by the Permian Period (Palaeozoic Era) and succeeded by the Jurassic Period (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 2.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Turonian Age is a division of geological time within the Cretaceous Period. It is the second of the six ages within the Late Cretaceous Epoch. It is preceded by the Cenomanian Age and succeeded by the Coniacian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Ufimian-Kazanian Age is a deprecated term, used for Permian rocks on the Russian Platform, approximately equating to the upper Kungurian Age - Roadian Age interval (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 24.9).

Upper Pleistocene Age (unnamed) is a division of geological time within the Quaternary Period. It is the last of the four ages within the Pleistocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Chibanian Age and succeeded by the Holocene Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 30.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/). Replaces: Tarantian Age.

Valanginian Age is a division of geological time within the Cretaceous Period. It is the second of the six ages within the Early Cretaceous Epoch. It is preceded by the Berriasian Age and succeeded by the Hauterivian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 27.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Velfreyan Substage is a substage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of two substages of the Aurelucian Stage. It is preceded by the Llandeilian Stage and succeeded by the Costonian Substage (BGS Research Report RR/12/04, table 1).

Visean Age is a division of geological time within the Carboniferous Period. It is the only age within the Mid Mississippian Epoch. It is preceded by the Tournaisian Age (Early Mississippian Epoch) and succeeded by the Serpukhovian Age (Late Mississippian Epoch). The Visean is also the second of six stages comprising the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme, preceded by the Tournaisian Stage and succeeded by the Namurian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 23.5; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Volgian Stage is a deprecated term, a European regional stage approximately equating to the Tithonian Age (Jurassic Period) - earliest Berriasian Age (Cretaceous Period) interval (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 26.9).

Waalian Stage is an Early Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a temporate (interglacial) interval. It is preceded by the Eburonian Stage and succeeded by the Menapian Stage. It is contemporaneous with part of the Beestonian Stage in Great Britain (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).
Waltonian Age is a deprecated Neogene term, replaced by Piacenzian Age.

Weichselian Stage is the last Late Pleistocene stage in the NW European Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a cold (glacial) interval. It is preceded by the Eemian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Devensian Stage in Great Britain (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b).

Wenlock Epoch is the second of the four epochs of the Silurian Period. It is preceded by the Llandovery Epoch and succeeded by the Ludlow Epoch (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 21.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Westphalian Stage is the fourth of six stages of the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is preceded by the Namurian Stage and succeeded by the Stephanian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).
Westphalian Substage A is a deprecated W European Carboniferous term, replaced by Langsettian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).
Westphalian Substage B is a deprecated W European Carboniferous term, replaced by Duckmantian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).
Westphalian Substage C is a deprecated W European Carboniferous term, replaced by Bolsovian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).
Westphalian Substage D is a deprecated W European Carboniferous term, replaced by Asturian Substage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Whitlandian Stage is a stage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the second of three stages of the Arenig Series. It is preceded by the Moridunian Stage and succeeded by the Fennian Stage (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 20.12).

Windermere Interstadial is a relatively warm period near the end of the Devensian Stage. It is preceded by the Dimlington Stadial and succeeded by the Loch Lomond Stadial (BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b; BGS British Regional Geology: Northern England (Fifth edition), fig. 64).

Wolstonian Stage is a Mid Pleistocene stage in the British Quaternary climatostratigraphic scheme. It is interpreted as a cold (glacial) interval. It is preceded by the Hoxnian Stage and succeeded by the Ipswichian Stage. It is contemporaneous with the Saalian Stage of NW Europe, and with marine isotope stages 6-10 (Geologic Time Scale 2020, fig. 30.2; BGS Research Report RR/10/003, table 1b). It is named for the village of Wolston, Warwickshire, England.

Woolstonian Substage is a substage in the British regional Ordovician stratigraphic scheme. It is the first of two substages of the Cheneyan Stage. It is preceded by the Longvillian Substage (Burrellian Stage) and succeeded by the Marshbrookian Substage (BGS Research Report RR/12/04, table 1).

Wordian Age is a division of geological time within the Permian Period. It is the second of the three ages within the Guadalupian Epoch. It is preceded by the Roadian Age and succeeded by the Capitanian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Wuchiapingian Age is a division of geological time within the Permian Period. It is the first of the two ages within the Lopingian Epoch. It is preceded by the Capitanian Age (Guadalupian Epoch) and succeeded by the Changhsingian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 24.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Wuliuan Age is a division of geological time within the Cambrian Period. It is the first of the three ages within the Miaolingian Epoch. It is preceded by Cambrian Stage 4 (of Cambrian Series 2) and succeeded by the Drumian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 19.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Yeadonian Substage is a substage in the British regional Carboniferous stratigraphic scheme. It is the last of seven substages of the Namurian Stage. It is preceded by the Marsdenian Substage and succeeded by the Langsettian Substage (Westphalian Stage) (Geologic Time scale 2020, fig. 23.5).

Ypresian Age is a division of geological time within the Paleogene Period. It is the first of the four ages within the Eocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Thanetian Age (Paleocene Epoch) and succeeded by the Lutetian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 28.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).

Zanclean Age is a division of geological time within the Neogene Period. It is the first of the two ages within the Pliocene Epoch. It is preceded by the Messinian Age (Miocene Epoch) and succeeded by the Piacenzian Age (Geologic Time Scale 2020, figs. 2.1, 29.1; https://timescalefoundation.org/).
